What changed since the last view: the numbers no longer count Frattesi or Gudmundsson as missing, but Sky and Corriere dello Sport say Frattesi came back from Italy with fatigue and may only be on the bench, Gudmundsson is fit but short of match fitness and should come on later, and Gattuso is managing minutes ahead of the derby and the Supercoppa. Lecce are without Pierotti and Ilic, with Monteiro and Berisha to be assessed; referee Matteo Marcenaro's high card rate (4.5 a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals, already cut for Zaccagni (-10.5%) and Tavares, and now assuming Frattesi and Gudmundsson are available. Reports say Frattesi may start on the bench and Gudmundsson only come on late, with Gattuso protecting players before the derby, so Lazio's attack is a little lighter than the numbers think; a mild lean down to about 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Without Zaccagni and Tavares Lazio lose their most direct left side, while Lecce have won plenty of corners lately (33 in six); the numbers already see both, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards and already add Marcenaro's high rate (+19%) while taking some off for Lazio's calm recent run. Lecce fighting near the bottom away at the leaders could bring tactical fouls, but there is no rivalry or ban threat reported, so I stay at about 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.7 shots. Frattesi, Lazio's midfielder who shoots most from deep, is likely to start on the bench and Gudmundsson to play only a part, so I nudge it down slightly to about 25.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target, with Lecce's sharp recent shooting (34 on target in six) already counted. With Frattesi and Gudmundsson likely limited to the bench, Lazio's front line (Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin) carries the threat alone; about 8.4.

401874967.overall: Parma (16th, one win in five) host Roma (3rd, 27 points, 21 goals in their last six). Gilardino's defence is in crisis: Ndiaye is suspended and Romero out (both counted), but Diego Carlos is injured too and Drobnic is reported injured by SportParma while Tuttosport still lists him in the XI; Gilardino is even weighing a switch to a back four with Britschgi, Delprato, Troilo and Valeri. Gasperini gets Svilar back in goal (fit, though still some discomfort kicking) and Dybala is expected to start behind or next to Malen, with only Pellegrini and Rensch missing (counted). Referee Simone Sozza's above-average card rate (4.2 a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and already take Romero off Parma (-14%) and lift Roma for their scoring run. A patched-up Parma back line without Diego Carlos (and maybe Drobnic) facing a Roma attack with Dybala back is something the numbers can't see; a mild lean up to about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already add Roma's strong recent corner count (+9%). Roma's wing-backs Molina and Wesley push high in Gasperini's system, but that is already in their numbers, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already add Sozza's record (4.2 a game). Troilo playing on a booking from a ban may make him a little careful, and there is no rivalry here, so I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already raised a lot for Roma's recent shooting (+26%). Parma's weakened defence points up, but the numbers are already high, so I stay at about 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Dybala's return gives Roma more quality in the final third against a Parma back line missing Diego Carlos as well as Ndiaye; a small nudge to about 9.7.

401875067.overall: Napoli (10th, 15 points, one win in five) host Torino (11th, 14 points) in a mid-table game. Allegri's injury list keeps growing: Lobotka, Di Lorenzo, Badiashile and Alisson Santos (counted) plus Buongiorno, and on Thursday goalkeeper Meret fractured a lumbar vertebra in training, so Milinkovic-Savic starts in goal; Sky says 19 of 26 players have had physical problems this season. Neres is back but should start on the bench and Spinazzola and Favasuli return; one report says De Bruyne could be rested, but Goal, DAZN and Cuore Toro have him starting. Torino's Vlasic has a thigh problem and is doubtful (counted as out), while Abate gets Ricardo Rodriguez and Belghali back. Referee Antonio Rapuano's very high card rate (5.1 a game) is already in the numbers, so the view stays with them.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, already cut for Lobotka, Di Lorenzo and Vlasic and raised for Napoli's leaky defence lately (14 conceded in six). Milinkovic-Savic replacing Meret is a like-for-like swap rather than a clear weakness, and De Bruyne most likely starts, so I stay at about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Napoli have won few corners lately (21 in six) but Torino concede plenty; Neres coming off the bench could add width late on, which is not enough to move it, so I stay at about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and already add Rapuano's high rate (+32%). There is no rivalry or ban threat reported and both sides have been calm lately, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots, already lifted for Torino's shooting against a Napoli side conceding many chances. Napoli's absences in midfield and at the back are counted, and Torino may switch between a back three and four, which changes little, so I stay at about 27.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. McTominay, Hojlund and Lang are expected to start, most reports also have De Bruyne, close to what the numbers assume, so I stay at about 8.8.

401875008.overall: Juventus (7th, 18 points, LWLWD) host 19th-placed Venezia in the Sunday lunch game, needing a win after dropping points against lower-table sides. Spalletti is expected to use a back three (Gatti, Bremer, Lucumi) with McKennie and Cabal on the flanks because of knocks: Cambiaso, Celik and Nico Gonzalez are still being assessed, and Kalulu, Locatelli, Khephren Thuram, Grabara and Yildiz are out (Yildiz since August, so already absent from the numbers' recent games). Venezia under Davide Nicola play a compact, aggressive 3-5-2 built for counter-attacks through Yeboah and Akor Adams; Franjic is out and Sverko and Adorante are being assessed. Referee Alberto Arena has a low card record on a tiny sample (3 games), which the numbers already blend in.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I drop last view's small lean up: Juve are short of their usual wide players (Cambiaso, Celik and Nico Gonzalez doubtful) and Venezia will sit in a dense midfield, which offsets Juve's need to win, so I stay at about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, already raised for Juve's recent corner count (+12%). Venezia defending deep should give Juve plenty of corners, but that is what the numbers already show, so I stay at about 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards, cut for both teams' quiet recent run and for Arena's low record on only three games. Nicola's sides defend aggressively and Venezia are fighting relegation, which a small referee sample can't capture; a mild lean up to about 2.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.4 shots, already lifted for Venezia's recent shooting (+18%). Juve will have the ball, but without their best wide players and against a compact block that is close to what the numbers expect, so I stay at about 30.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Juve's front three (Kolo Muani, Woltemade and Alajbegovic or Boga) is the expected one and their recent accuracy is already counted, so I stay at about 8.9.

401875047.overall: In-form Bologna (8th, four straight wins under Palladino) host bottom side Udinese (5 points), who sacked Runjaic in early November and are now coached by Paolo Zanetti, who has had the international break to work with the squad. Bologna miss Holm (counted) and left wing-back Juan Miranda (hamstring), a key crosser who is not on the numbers' list, with Alhassane replacing him; Cambiaghi, who the numbers count as available, is still doubtful after an ankle knock. Udinese miss Gueye and Bertola (both counted), while Alaba and Zanoli are being assessed. Referee Livio Marinelli's average card record (3.6 a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, already lifted for Bologna's scoring run (+5%) and cut for Gueye. Miranda, Bologna's main supplier from the left, is out and Cambiaghi is doubtful, neither of which the numbers count; a mild lean down to about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Bologna's wide play continues through Zortea and Alhassane, and Udinese under Zanetti are expected to defend with a back three, close to what the numbers assume, so I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already count Marinelli's average record. Udinese have been calm (7 cards in six) and a new coach may want discipline; nothing new points either way, so I stay at about 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots. Without Miranda and possibly Cambiaghi, Bologna lose two of their attacking outlets, which the numbers don't know; a small nudge down to about 25.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, already raised for Bologna's sharp recent shooting (+16%). Orsolini and Odgaard or Piccoli are expected to lead the line as usual, so I stay at about 8.8.

401874960.overall: Sassuolo (17th, five straight defeats) sacked Alberto Aquilani and Roberto D'Aversa takes charge for the first time, with solidity his stated priority. Berardi, Volpato and Adzic, all counted out by the numbers, are still doubtful and Goal expects Berardi to miss out; Ismael Kone, Leysen and Boloca are unavailable too, and Dominguez or Bowie could start on the right. Genoa (13th, four wins in their last six) under De Rossi have almost the whole squad, with only Frendrup a doubt, and are praised for their compactness. Referee Maria Sole Ferrieri Caputi has a one-game Serie A record here, which the numbers blend toward the average.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, already cut heavily for Sassuolo's missing attackers (Adzic, Berardi, Volpato). A new coach's first game usually brings a tighter, more cautious side, and D'Aversa has said protecting the goal comes first, against a compact Genoa; a mild lean down to about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. A more cautious Sassuolo might defend deeper, but Genoa have won few corners lately (20 in six), so the two pull in opposite directions; I stay at about 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, with a referee record of one game that tells little. A first game under a new coach in a relegation scrap tends to bring more duels and tactical fouls; a small lean up to about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. D'Aversa's focus on short distances between the lines and defending transitions, plus Sassuolo's missing forwards, points to a slower game with fewer chances; about 23.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already low for Sassuolo's poor shooting lately (14 on target in six). The same cautious start under D'Aversa nudges it down slightly, to about 8.

401874989.overall: Milan (4th, 24 points) host surprise side Frosinone (6th, 20 points), whose 24 goals are among the league's best and who lost 1-0 at Cagliari before the break. Frosinone miss top scorer Raimondo, Grillitsch and the suspended Bracaglia, with Terzic doubtful, all counted by the numbers; Birligea or Bobcek leads the line. Amorim's defence is stretched: Tomori and Gabbia are out and Pavlovic's chances are described as very low after a kidney problem, while Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze are also out; Tomori and Pavlovic are not on the numbers' list. Maignan should start after a knock with France, and referee Luca Pairetto, one of the strictest in Serie A (4.9 cards a game), is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already cut a lot for Raimondo (-19% on Frosinone's goals). Milan's back line without Tomori and very likely Pavlovic, neither counted, faces a Frosinone side that shoots a lot; a mild lean up to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, already raised for Frosinone's big recent corner count (+9.5%). Milan's makeshift defence doesn't change how either side gets to the byline, so I stay at about 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards and already add Pairetto's strict record (+35%). There is no rivalry and no ban threat reported, so I stay at about 5.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.3 shots, already lifted heavily for Frosinone's shooting (+24%). That is high enough, so I stay at about 33.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target. A Milan defence missing Tomori and probably Pavlovic should let Frosinone get more efforts on goal; a small nudge to about 11.1.

401875541.overall: Mid-table NEC (11th, 14 pts) host leaders PSV (26 pts) after the international break, with PSV one point clear of Feyenoord and needing a win to stay top. NEC beat Utrecht 3-2 last time with Dusan Tadic back from his calf injury, and the last six meetings were high-scoring (NEC won the last two, 3-2 and 3-2). NEC still miss Bram Nuytinck and centre-back Perr Schuurs (hamstring, not on the numbers' list), with Dennis Geiger (25%) and Emre Mor (50%) doubtful; the numbers treat Geiger and Mor as out. For PSV, Nagalo, Schouten and Plea are out (counted) plus Sami Ouaissa; Sergino Dest is a 50/50 doubt after leaving the US camp early, but Soccernews expects Bosz to change only one player, with Filip Kostic at left-back and Ivan Perisic (75%) on the wing. Referee Jeroen Manschot's above-average card rate is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, already including NEC's hot scoring run (14 in six), small cuts for Mor, Geiger and Plea, and a little for the high-scoring head-to-head. What they can't see is NEC playing without centre-back Perr Schuurs on top of Nuytinck against PSV's league-best attack (40 goals), while Tadic is fit to lead NEC's own attack. A mild +3% to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, with NEC's recent corner surge (+2%) and PSV's quieter spell (-5%) already counted. My earlier view cut this because PSV's crossers Dest and Kostic were doubts, but Kostic is now expected to start at left-back and only Dest remains 50/50, so I drop that cut and stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, already pushed up about 18% for referee Jeroen Manschot (3.5 cards a game in 51 games). No suspensions hang over either side and this is a normal leaders-away-at-midtable game without extra needle, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.4 shots, with NEC's heavy recent shooting (116 in six, +10%) already counted. Tadic back raises NEC's threat while PSV field an almost unchanged attacking line (Perisic, Mijnans, Van Bommel), so nothing moves the total and I stay at 29.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target, with NEC's sharper recent finishing already in. PSV's front line is close to full strength and NEC's patched defence is reflected in my small goals lean rather than here, so I stay at 11.0.

401875544.overall: Struggling Utrecht (14th, 12 pts, two points above the relegation zone) host promoted Cambuur (10th), who went eight games unbeaten before losing 5-2 at home to PSV. Utrecht have lost to Telstar and NEC, have conceded 34 league goals (second most), and coach Anthony Correia is under heavy pressure; former players quoted by Utrechtfans even call Cambuur the favourites. Utrecht miss Jonathans and Ohio (knee), Paredes and Engwanda, with Victor Jensen only 25%; Cambuur are without first-choice keeper Jasper Meijster (hand, out until March), captain Jamal Amofa and Daan Visser, with Wout Asselman a major doubt. Referee Allard Lindhout (3.2 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, already counting Cambuur's good scoring run (16 in six) and Utrecht's leaky defence (15 conceded in six). Cambuur's keeper Meijster is out until March, which the numbers list but give no goal effect, and pundits describe Utrecht as pressing without organisation and conceding on the counter; a mild +3% to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, most of them Utrecht's (6.4). A Utrecht side under pressure at home should push forward and Cambuur are happy to counter, but that is already the shape of the numbers, and the injury news on both sides doesn't affect wide play, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already lifted for Utrecht's 12 cards in their last six (+10%) and for referee Lindhout's slightly high rate. Fan anger at Utrecht could add some edge, but nothing concrete (suspensions, a rivalry) points to more, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots, with Utrecht expected to take 17.5. Utrecht are missing attackers Jonathans, Ohio and Paredes, but those absences have lasted for weeks and are in their recent shot counts, so I stay at 29.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, already trimming Utrecht for weaker recent accuracy (-6%) and lifting Cambuur (+8%). With no fresh team news on either attack, I stay at 10.4.

401875543.overall: Second-placed Feyenoord (25 pts, one behind PSV) host Excelsior (15th, 11 pts), who have lost five league games in a row, scored once in that run and failed to score in their last four, including a 9-0 defeat at Twente. Feyenoord are winless in five in all competitions and lost 5-3 at Heerenveen last time, conceding in each of their last five, so Giovanni van Bronckhorst needs a response. Their back line is thin: St. Juste (counted), Nieuwkoop, Bos, Beelen and Wessels are out, Moder is not back, Gijs Smal is 50/50 and winger Anis Hadj Moussa (ankle) is unlikely, while Reiss Nelson and Shaqueel van Persie are available again. Excelsior's Nesto Groen serves the last game of his ban (counted) and Aymen Sliti (thumb) expects to play. The numbers add a big derby boost for cards, but this Rotterdam derby is one-sided (Excelsior have not won at De Kuip since 1980) and not hostile, so I trim that.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, already counting Excelsior's collapse (22 conceded in six), St. Juste's absence and Groen's ban. Feyenoord have Nelson and Van Persie back in attack and a patched defence that has conceded in five straight games, but Excelsior have not scored in four league games, so I lean only slightly higher, to about 4.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Feyenoord taking most of them (6.8) and Excelsior's drop in corners already in the momentum adjustment. Hadj Moussa, Feyenoord's most direct winger, is unlikely to play, but Van Persie and Valente give other wide options, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, and that already includes a +39% derby boost plus referee Robin Hensgens' average record. This city derby is not a hostile one: Feyenoord have won their last six meetings, the clubs are on good terms, and a game with Feyenoord on the ball usually brings few home fouls. I trim it -6% to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with Feyenoord on 19.2 and Excelsior on just 9.1 after a dismal run (45 shots in six, already counted). Feyenoord's returning attackers support a high home total, but that is already the numbers' expectation, so I stay at 28.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target, already including Excelsior giving up many on-target shots and barely hitting the target themselves (9 in six). Sliti should play and Groen is banned, so Excelsior's threat stays small, as the numbers already assume; I stay at 10.9.

401875546.overall: The Derby of the North: Groningen (9th, one point from their last four, conceding at least two in each) against in-form Heerenveen (6th), who have won four in a row, the last a 5-3 comeback against Feyenoord. Groningen will be without coach Dick Lukkien, recovering from a hip replacement, so assistant Casper Goedkoop leads the side from the touchline. Keeper Etienne Vaessen and Hans Hateboer are banned after red cards at AZ, second keeper Rijk Janse is out long-term, so Lovro Stubljar is expected in goal; Malcolm Jeng and Travis Hernes are also out. Heerenveen have a fully fit squad. The bans, the derby and referee Alex Bos' slightly higher card rate are already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, already including both sides' scoring runs (17 goals each in six), Vaessen's ban (+6% for Heerenveen) and Hateboer's absence. Beyond what they count, Groningen go in with their third-choice keeper because Janse is also out, a defence pundits call vulnerable, and no head coach on the bench; a mild +3% to about 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, with Groningen's recent drop in corners already counted (-6%). Groningen are expected to press high from the start and Heerenveen to counter, which fits the numbers' even split, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already including a +39% derby boost and Alex Bos' slightly above-average record. This is a real rivalry, but both sides have been light on cards recently (counted), and nothing beyond the derby itself points higher, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, with Heerenveen's sharp recent shooting (+8%) counted. Groningen's high press and the space it leaves usually make for an open game, but that is the style the numbers have measured all season, so I stay at 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, with Heerenveen's recent accuracy (+7%) and Groningen's dip (-7%) already in. The keeper change affects how many go in rather than how many are on target, so I stay at 10.0.

401875539.overall: A game near the bottom: Telstar (16th, 10 pts) host PEC Zwolle (13th, 12 pts), both within three points of the relegation places. Telstar ended a ten-game winless run and have four points from their last two, but have conceded 17 in six home games and lost seven straight meetings with Zwolle; coach Henk Brugge's position is still described as insecure. PEC are unbeaten in four and this is Alex Pastoor's first league game as coach; he says the team needs little changing, and PEC won a friendly 1-0 against Heerenveen in his first match. Injury news conflicts: one tracker now lists Telstar's Gerald Alders and Rui Mendes as available, while Sports Mole says Alders is out and Mendes unlikely; PEC miss Rahajaan, with Floranus and Krastev doubtful. Referee Joey Kooij (3.4 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already counting Mendes out for Telstar (-3.5%) and Alders out of their defence (+6% for PEC). If both return, as one tracker suggests, the effects roughly cancel; my earlier cautious lean for Pastoor's debut fades now that he says he will keep the side that went unbeaten in four. Both teams keep few clean sheets (three in 24 between them), which the numbers already show, so I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Telstar's recent drop (-3%) already counted. Pastoor's set-up is unlikely to differ much from the caretakers', and nothing in Telstar's news points either way, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already including Joey Kooij's above-average record (+11%) and PEC's recent cards. It is a tense game between two sides near the drop, but that is common at this level and nothing specific points higher, so I drop my earlier small lean and stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already lifted for Telstar's busy recent shooting (+11%), led by Tyrone Owusu's run of four goals in six. Nothing in the team news changes either side's volume, so I stay at 30.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, with both sides' recent accuracy close to normal. I had shaded this down for a cautious new-coach game, but with Pastoor keeping PEC's set-up there is no reason to, so I stay at 10.6.

401875545.overall: Fourth-placed Twente (24 pts, two behind PSV) host bottom side Willem II, who have 3 points from 12 games, have conceded 40 goals and have not won in 29 Eredivisie matches; another winless game would equal the league record held by Helmond Sport (1983-84). Willem II replaced John Stegeman with Jurgen Streppel in October and have since lost 7-0 at PSV and drawn 1-1 with PEC; keeper Thomas Didillon was listed 50/50 by an injury tracker, and Hoogma and Lachkar are out (counted). The same tracker lists Jaden Slory's one-match ban as ending before this game, so my earlier trim for his absence is removed. Twente's Thorvaldsen, Bruns and Lemkin are only 25% and keeper Unnerstall 50%; the numbers take off only a little for Bruns. Serdar Gozubuyuk's high card rate (+37%) is already a big part of the cards number.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals, already lifted for Twente's 21 goals in their last six and Willem II's 21 conceded. My earlier small trim was for Slory's ban, but he appears to have served it, and Twente's doubtful attackers (Thorvaldsen, Bruns) are offset by Willem II possibly missing keeper Didillon, so I stay at 4.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners, already up for Twente's 46 corners in six games (+6%) and down for Willem II's low output. A one-sided game with Twente camped in Willem II's half is exactly what those figures describe, so I stay at 10.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, with referee Serdar Gozubuyuk's 3.9 a game (+37%) already pushing it well above average and Willem II's 12 cards in six counted too. A side chasing a game often picks up cards, but that is already priced in, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 35.6 shots, already lifted strongly for Twente's 145 shots in six (+25%) and cut for Willem II's low output. That covers the expected siege, and Twente's doubtful forwards being out changes who shoots rather than how often, so I stay at 35.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, already up for Twente's accuracy (+14%) and down for Willem II's (-9%). With no new absences confirmed on either side, I drop my earlier small trim and stay at 11.2.

401875547.overall: Third-placed Ajax (25 pts) host ADO Den Haag (17th, 9 pts), who sacked Robin Peter on 2 November and beat Sparta 3-1 under interim coach Levi Schwiebbe. The numbers take a big cut off Ajax for Julian Brandt (-13%) and Kasper Dolberg (-7%); Dolberg is out for the season, and Brandt is now a real doubt: he trains only in a limited way and an injury tracker rates him 25%, the same as Steven Berghuis, while Amrabat, Kehrer and Gaaei are back in full training. ADO miss Pozo and Reischl (counted), with keeper Kilian Nikiema 50/50 and defender Pascal Mulder 75%, which the numbers do not see. Ajax play in the Conference League in midweek and visit Feyenoord on 29 November, but a strong home side is expected. Referee Erwin Blank shows slightly fewer cards than average, which is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals with Brandt taken off completely (-13% for Ajax). He is now only an outside chance to play, so I give back only a little of that cut, plus a touch for ADO possibly missing first-choice keeper Nikiema; together about +2% to 3.2. My earlier +5% assumed Brandt was likely to play.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Ajax's slightly low recent corner count and ADO's normal output already counted. Ajax will have most of the ball against a side near the bottom, which the 6.7 home corners already reflect, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, already nudged up for both sides' recent cards and down for Erwin Blank's lighter touch (-5%). Nothing new on suspensions or tension points either way, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.1 shots, already up for Ajax's recent volume (+9%) and ADO's (+7%). With Brandt unlikely, Ajax lose their main creator, which the numbers already assume, so I drop my earlier small lean and stay at 34.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target. Brandt has a small chance of playing, which the numbers rule out, and Amrabat, Kehrer and Gaaei are back to give Ajax a stronger base; a small +2% to about 10.7.

401875540.overall: Sparta (12th, 12 pts) host AZ (5th, 23 pts), who have won only one of their last five league games (4-3 against Groningen) and visit Sparta Prague in the Europa League next. AZ's absences go beyond what the numbers know: besides Hornkamp, Zoet and Resink (counted), Kees Smit is out for weeks after a groin setback (NH Nieuws), Weslley Patati and Lewis Schouten are injured, and Wouter Goes and keeper Owusu-Oduro are 50/50. Sparta lost 3-1 at ADO before the break and are without keeper Michael Brouwer (ankle), Nick Verschuren and Teo Quintero, with Julian Baas (ill) likely to play; the numbers list no Sparta absences. Referee Ingmar Oostrom's slightly above-average card rate is already counted. News for this specific match was thin; the view rests mostly on the injury lists and form.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already taking about 5% off AZ for Hornkamp and counting Sparta's 16 conceded in six. AZ's extra absences (Patati, Smit, Schouten) weaken their attack, while Sparta are without keeper Brouwer and defender Verschuren, which helps AZ; the two roughly cancel, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, with AZ's low corners conceded and Sparta's normal output already counted. Nothing in the team news changes how wide either side plays, so I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, already pushed up for Sparta's 14 cards in six (+8%) and for Ingmar Oostrom (3.3 a game). No suspensions or extra needle are reported, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, with AZ's recent 93 shots in six counted (+8%). AZ are short of attacking depth with winger Patati, Schouten and the creative Smit out on top of Hornkamp, and a European trip follows, so I trim slightly to about 28.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, already lifted a little for AZ's accuracy (+6%). With fewer options in AZ's attack than the numbers assume, I shade it to about 9.9.

401875542.overall: Go Ahead Eagles (8th, 17 pts) host Fortuna Sittard (7th, 20 pts), who have drawn five of their last six, most recently 2-2 at home to Telstar. Fortuna are badly hit: Ole Romeny, Lequincio Zeefuik, Edouard Michut, centre-back Rodrigo Guth and Daley Sinkgraven are all out until December or January, and the brief lists no Fortuna absences, so the numbers do not see them (their recent momentum partly does). Go Ahead won 1-0 at Excelsior last time; Marsman and Saathof are out as the numbers know. Referee Martijn Vos (4.6 cards a game) is already a large part of the cards number. Match-specific previews were thin; this view rests on the injury lists and form.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Fortuna are without forwards Romeny and Zeefuik and midfielder Michut, none of whom the numbers take off, and have scored only 8 in their last six (partly counted). Guth's absence weakens their defence a little, which pulls the other way, so I trim to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, already cut a little for Fortuna's low recent corner count (20 in six). Go Ahead should press and push down the wings as usual, and Fortuna's absences are already showing in that low count, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards: Martijn Vos's very high card rate (+40%) pushes it up, while Go Ahead's 4 cards in their last six and Fortuna's low count pull it down, all already counted. Nothing new on discipline, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots. Fortuna's shooting is down recently (64 in six, counted) and they are missing several attacking players the numbers don't know about, so I lean lower to about 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. With Romeny, Zeefuik and Michut out, Fortuna should test Go Ahead's keeper less than the numbers assume; about 9.3.

401875001.overall: Atalanta (12th, 14 points, one win in five) host second-placed Inter (28 points, four wins in five), with Sarri's side well short of last season's level and Chivu's Inter chasing the top spot. What changed: Thuram is now expected to start with Pio Esposito, while Lautaro Martinez is back from his hamstring injury but should only come off the bench; Bonny and Stankovic are out (only Stankovic is counted). On the other side, DAZN lists centre-backs Hien and Kossounou plus Pompei as unavailable and Scalvini is not fully recovered from international duty, none of it in the numbers, which list no Atalanta absences. Referee Fabio Maresca (4.8 cards a game) has now been named and his record is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I drop last view's lean down: Inter's attack is less thin than feared, with Thuram starting and Lautaro available from the bench, and Atalanta's defence is missing Hien and Kossounou, which the numbers don't know; the two roughly cancel, so I stay at about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, already raised for Inter's recent corner count against an Atalanta side conceding many. Nothing in the team news changes the wide play of either side, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards and already add Maresca's high rate (+26%) and a lively head-to-head (+13%). No suspension threat or new rivalry angle has been reported, so I stay at about 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots. Atalanta's weakened centre-back pairing points up for Inter and Lautaro being only on the bench points slightly down, so nothing clear moves it; about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Thuram and Esposito up front with Lautaro to come on is close to Inter's usual threat, and Atalanta's missing defenders could help them, so I stay at about 9.3.

401876400.overall: Marseille (4th, 18 points) have won five league games in a row under Bruno Genesio and have 22 goals, joint-most in Ligue 1, while promoted Le Mans (15th, 8 points) are winless in five and have conceded in every league game. Marseille had no injuries from the international break, with Højbjerg, Aguerd, Gouiri and Abdelli fit, and only Emerson (knee arthroscopy) and Cornelius out, both counted. Le Mans are without Bourabaa and Sidibé, with Rossignol, Eyoum and Brahimi doubtful and captain Yohou to be checked after a head knock, so they may travel depleted. Marseille host Levski Sofia in the Europa League on Thursday, and referee Eric Wattellier (3.5 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already take a large share off Le Mans for Bourabaa. Marseille are in form and at full strength apart from two defenders, and Le Mans have more doubts than the numbers know, but a European game on Thursday may mean some game management once Marseille lead; these balance out, so I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.1 corners. Le Mans' back five and Marseille's narrow attacking midfield (Harit, Abdelli) are already in the numbers, so I stay at 8.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already take some off for Wattellier's lenient record. With part of the Virage Sud closed and no rivalry here, nothing points either way, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots. Le Mans may travel depleted with several doubts the numbers do not know, which should let an in-form Marseille side camp in their half, so I nudge it up to about 26.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Marseille's attack is unchanged and scoring every week, which the numbers already show, so I stay at 9.3.

401882803.overall: Getafe (15th, 12 pts) host Atlético Madrid (3rd, 28 pts) on Sunday night; Getafe are under pressure in the table and Atlético are a side Bordalás rarely beats. Gudelj is banned (in the numbers) and Zaid Romero is racing to be fit, with Valiu the alternative. Atlético are without Lookman (knee sprain with Nigeria), whom the numbers now count, while Pubill (mild ankle sprain) is unlikely and Cuti Romero (adductor, out since 17 October) has a better chance but may be spared; Atlético have won only four of 13 without Romero. Barrios and Hancko are back, Grimaldo came home early with a fever, and several internationals returned late with a Champions League game on Tuesday. No referee had been named in the pages I read.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and now take Lookman off, so I no longer size his absence. What's left that they can't see: Atlético's internationals returned late, Grimaldo has been ill, and Simeone may manage the game before Tuesday, while Bordalás's Getafe make home games slow and tight. A small lean down to about 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already count Getafe's high recent corner count (38 in six games). Getafe play direct and win corners from long balls and crosses at home, while Atlético have a bit less pace out wide without Lookman, which the numbers count. Nothing points clearly either way, so 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, counting both teams' card form and past meetings, but the game is not flagged as a derby. It is a Madrid-area meeting against a Bordalás side built on fouls, duels and slowing the game, and these meetings tend to get heated. With no referee named yet, a mild lean up to about 5.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.6 shots, and recent form has already pushed both sides up (+13% Getafe, +8% Atlético). Getafe rely on long balls and rarely build many shots, and Atlético are likely to manage the game with tired internationals and the Champions League on Tuesday. Lookman is now in the numbers, so I trim less than before, to about 23.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 shots on target. A slow, stop-start game with Atlético managing their effort before Tuesday should mean few clear chances, while Lookman's absence is already counted. A slight lean down to about 7.2.

401883111.overall: Sixth-placed Burgos (24 points) host 19th-placed Albacete (13 points) on Sunday night at El Plantío. Burgos, under Sergio Francisco, saw a four-game unbeaten run end with a 3-1 loss at Leganés; they are a set-piece threat who fill the box, but are without forwards Jon Karrikaburu and David González and also Brais Martínez, of whom only González is in the numbers. Albacete have been transformed under Joseba Etxeberria, with four straight league wins (latest 1-0 v Celta Fortuna), a high press and quick counters, though they are still in the bottom four. Albacete miss Puertas, Obeng, Fran Gámez, Higinio Marín, Javi Moreno and the suspended José Corpas, most of them out for weeks; striker Munir is close to returning and Sanba has ankle inflammation. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take about 11% off Burgos's goals for David González. Karrikaburu is out too and the numbers don't know it, leaving Burgos short of forwards against an Albacete side that has kept things tight during its winning run, so I trim a little, to about 2.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 5.5 of them Burgos's, a side that attacks wide with quick full-backs and lives off set pieces. Albacete's press could push Burgos into more long balls, but that does not clearly change corners, so I stay at 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards. Albacete's pressing and Burgos's physical centre-backs could mean some duels, but nothing suggests extra needle and no referee is named, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, 17 of them Burgos's. With Karrikaburu and Brais Martínez out beyond what the numbers know, and Albacete's high press making Burgos play longer, I expect fewer home shots and trim to about 25.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Burgos's missing forwards should mean slightly fewer clear chances, so I trim a little, to about 7.8.

401883110.overall: Bottom against top at the Alfonso Murube on Monday night: Ceuta are last with 5 points from 14 games, eight from safety, and lost 2-0 at Tenerife in Sergio Lobera's first game after José Juan Romero was sacked. Almería, under Xavier García Pimienta, lead with 32 points, are unbeaten in 11 and have the best defence (11 conceded), with Miguel de la Fuente the league's top scorer on nine. Lobera now has a full week to bring in his possession and pressing ideas; at Tenerife Ceuta had about 64% of the ball but few clear chances and conceded on a counter and from a corner. Almería get Marcos Luna back from a ban and Dzodic and Cipenga back from international duty, with only Ely and Melamed out; Ceuta's Edgar Sevikyan went off injured at Tenerife with no update since. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, 1.2 of them Ceuta's, helped by last season's 3-2 home win in the head-to-head. I lean slightly lower, to about 3.2: Ceuta have scored 10 in 14 and under Lobera had the ball at Tenerife but little presence in the box, Sevikyan is a doubt after going off injured, and Almería have conceded only 11 all season. Almería's own scoring (De la Fuente in form, 13 in their last six) is already in the numbers.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.1 of them Ceuta's, which already includes their recent run of winning lots of corners (+11.4% momentum). Lobera's possession style fits that pattern rather than changing it, and Almería tend to let opponents have the ball, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already counting Ceuta's heavy recent booking (+12% momentum). Ceuta are desperate and at Tenerife were booked for stopping counters when their press was beaten, which is the same pattern; no referee has been named yet, so I stay at 6.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots, with Ceuta's recent shot volume already adding a large 30% to their side. Under Lobera they kept the ball and shot from range (Kuki Zalazar), while Almería tend to need few chances; that fits what the numbers already expect, so I stay at 31.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. In line with my goals lean I take a little off, to about 10.0: Ceuta managed only two on target at Tenerife despite most of the ball, their shooting is mostly from distance, and Sevikyan may be missing; Almería's own accuracy and their solid defence are already in the numbers.

401875009.overall: A meeting of two struggling sides on Monday night: Monza (Ivan Juric) are 18th with 7 points and have lost four of their last five, while Fiorentina (Paolo Vanoli) are 15th with 9 points after three games unbeaten (2-2 Atalanta, 4-2 Sassuolo, 2-2 Juventus). Both have scored 17 and conceded 25 in 11 games, so open, leaky games are the norm for both. Monza rely on Gustavo Varela, the league's top scorer; Folorunsho is back from a calf problem, but captain Pessina, Robinson (muscle problem from England U20 duty), Ngonge, Ciurria and Mout carry fitness doubts. Fiorentina miss Pongracic and Parisi, Atta and Ndour are close to returning, and Njie came back from Sweden duty with a thigh knock (Gnonto would replace him). The brief lists no missing players for either side, and no referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, and they already add a little for both sides' recent scoring and leaky defending (+2.6% each way). Both teams average about 3.8 goals per game between them this season, but knocks to attackers on both sides (Robinson and Ngonge for Monza, Njie for Fiorentina) and the relegation tension pull the other way, so I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, already nudging up for Fiorentina's recent corner count. Monza's wing-back 3-4-2-1 (Birindelli and Mangas wide) and Fiorentina's 4-2-3-1 don't point either way beyond what the numbers see, so I stay at 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, with recent card form already counted and no referee named yet. This is a scrap near the bottom: Monza are in the relegation zone and a win would lift them past Fiorentina, and the brief carries no stakes flag for it, so I lean mildly higher, to about 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, already raised strongly for both sides' recent shooting (+9% Monza, +13% Fiorentina). With Monza's supporting attackers Robinson and Ngonge and Fiorentina's Njie all carrying knocks, and Fiorentina's six internationals back only late in the week, I trim it slightly to about 28.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, already lifted around 10% for each side's recent form. For the same reasons as shots (attacking knocks on both sides, late returns from international duty) I trim it slightly to about 9.7; Varela, Monza's main threat, is fit and starts.

401879237.overall: Brentford (8th, 14 pts) host Everton (6th, 16 pts) on Monday night after the international break, two mid-table sides with only two points between them. Brentford lost 2-0 at Brighton last time after Igor Thiago, their main striker, was sent off for violent conduct; the appeal was rejected and his three-match ban starts here, which the numbers already count. Brentford are also without Rico Henry, Josh Dasilva and Kaye Furo, while Fabio Carvalho was ruled out until after the break and may be back. Everton came from behind to beat Coventry 3-1 with Thierno Barry scoring twice, report no injuries, and Jack Grealish is back in training after a disciplinary absence but David Moyes has not said whether he will play. No referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Without Thiago Brentford have no obvious centre-forward (predicted line-ups leave the slot open, with Schade the likeliest to move inside), but the numbers already take his absence off, about -12.5% on Brentford's goals. Grealish could give Everton more craft if he returns, but his place is not confirmed, so I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners. Brentford have won fewer corners than usual in their last six (21 against about 28 expected) and Everton a few more, which the numbers already count through form. I found nothing in the team news that changes how either side will attack wide, so I stay at 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, with Everton slightly more likely to pick them up. No referee had been named, so the numbers use average refereeing, and recent card form and past meetings are already counted. Nothing in the build-up points to a bad-tempered game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots. They take Thiago's ban off Brentford's goals but not off their shots, and he is the side's main shot-taker with no like-for-like replacement while Carvalho is only just coming back. Grealish's possible return pulls a little the other way for Everton, so I lean only mildly lower: about 26.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. Brentford have already been hitting the target less than usual (19 in their last six against about 25 expected), which the numbers count, and losing Thiago, their most direct finisher, should cut that a little more. I go mildly lower, to about 8.0.

401882802.overall: A Monday-night relegation derby of the Valencian region: Levante (17th, 11 pts) host Elche (18th, 10 pts), one point apart, with Elche in the drop zone after defeats to Valencia and Betis and without a win at the Ciutat de València in 33 years. Levante have kept no clean sheet in their last five home games; Brugué (5 goals) leads their attack and left-back Manu Sánchez is back from a hamstring problem. Martín Anselmi's Elche keep the ball and cross a lot for Fer Niño (6 goals); Marc Aguado (ankle) is out until mid-December, Lemar, Villar and Sangaré are reported close to fit but not certain, and Houary and Yago Santiago have knocks. The numbers list no missing players for this game and do not flag it as a derby; no referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already high for two bottom-four sides, because Levante concede a lot at home and Elche create plenty. A tense six-pointer could make both sides careful, but Levante have not kept a home clean sheet in five and Elche's Aguado has been out for a month, so his absence is already in their recent form. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, 4.9 of them Levante's. Anselmi's Elche keep the ball and lean on crosses to Fer Niño, which the numbers already see in their 31 corners in six games, while Levante have won fewer than expected lately. Nothing new in the team news changes that, so I keep 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, low because Levante have been booked little lately (11 in six). This is a regional derby and a direct relegation fight between two sides a point apart, which the numbers do not flag, and games like that usually bring more fouls and bookings; Levante's Dela and Elche's Gonzalo Villar are one booking from a ban. No referee is named yet, so a clear but moderate lean up to about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting (Levante conceded 103 in six games). Elche's possession game and Levante's leaky home record keep it high, but a nervy six-pointer could also slow it down. Nothing in the news points clearly either way, so I keep 29.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Brugué and Fer Niño, each side's top scorer, are both fit, and Elche's doubts (Lemar, Houary) are about creators who have missed games already, so their recent output counts it. I keep 8.9.
